coachNotes:
*Primary note/strategy from my advisor
A 4% withdrawal rule is a reasonable starting point. If you have $1.65M and draw 4% ($66k) alongside Social Security, that covers the $90k target. Plan for the conservative case and be pleasantly surprised if markets cooperate.

*Vehicle Notes
Term Life - pure protection while the kids are young, no cash value
Whole Life - cash value builds tax-deferred, can borrow against it if needed
Johnny's College Fund - savings earmarked for Johnny's tuition, college starts in about 10 years, not part of the retirement plan in spirit
401k - the main growth engine

*To Dos
Contribute to the 401k at least up to the full employer match first
Then keep funding the Whole Life cash value
userConcerns: I feel slightly behind on saving for my own retirement, but I know I have a pretty solid plan for Johnny in his college fund. He starts college in about 10 years. I am starting to wonder whether I should put even more into the college fund, or whether I should be increasing my 401k contributions instead, or some blend of the two. My spouse also wants to keep our checking and savings liquid in case something happens.
